rationale: The workflow is a single Arduino Lint job (checkout plus arduino/arduino-lint-action) with no matrix, no explicit dependency installation or lockfile, no test suite, and no Bazel build. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply because there are no matrix jobs to cancel. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE does not apply because there is no dependency fetch step or lockfile to key a cache on. P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE is contraindicated: the weekly schedule exists expressly to catch breakage from new Arduino Lint rules, which is an external dependency/time-based requirement that needs fresh checks regardless of repository activity. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT are not supported as optimizations here: the ci_history shows every run succeeds in about 11-13 seconds with no runaway or slow-run evidence, so there is no demonstrated problem a job timeout would solve; adding one would be speculative rather than evidence-supported for this workflow. All remaining patterns require tests, builds, queues, Bazel, or ci-service controls that are absent or out of scope. Build and test coverage is preserved by making no change.
